bio: Former field medic who ran triage in the first hours after the exchange. She doesn't talk about what she saw, but her hands never shake.
Kept the municipal water plant running for three weeks after the grid fell. Came to the bunker when the last pipe froze.
Her family's greenhouse survived the initial blast. She knows which soil still grows and which poisons the roots.
Haunted by a patient lost on Day 1. Their hands still remember the cut they couldn't finish.
Empty bottles line their pockets. The old CVS still has their logbook — if they dare go alone.
They treated dogs before the war. Now the dogs glow, and something in them still wants to heal.
They used to sit across from people and wait. The bunker still needs someone who can listen when the walls start talking.
They buried the first dead after the exchange. Closure is a trench and a shovel and the quiet that follows.
Day 1 never ended for them. The old squad still calls on the radio — and something answers back.
They still wear the badge under the coat. The precinct lockbox is still there — if the streets allow it.
Door security before the war. Now the only door that matters is the hatch, and they still stand it alone.
They tracked game before the blast. Something white still moves out there — and only a bow feels honest.
Left to die when the walls opened. The Warden's keys still hang on a ghoul's belt inside the Penitentiary.
